answer_text:
Let the given angle be \(\angle AOB=19^\circ\), with vertex \(O\).

**Construction**

1. Draw a circle \(\omega\) centered at \(O\) with any radius. Let it meet \(OA\) at \(C\) and \(OB\) at \(D\).  
   The chord \(CD\) subtends the given angle \(19^\circ\) at \(O\).

2. With the compass set to the length \(CD\), step off **19 successive equal chords** on \(\omega\) in the direction from \(C\) to \(D\):
   \[
   C=P_0,\quad P_1=D,\quad P_2,\dots,P_{19}.
   \]
   Each chord \(P_{k-1}P_k\) subtends a central angle of \(19^\circ\).

3. Since
   \[
   19\cdot 19^\circ = 361^\circ = 360^\circ+1^\circ,
   \]
   the ray \(OP_{19}\) is \(1^\circ\) from the ray \(OC\). Thus the small chord \(CP_{19}\) subtends a central angle of \(1^\circ\).

4. Now set the compass to the small chord \(CP_{19}\). Step this length along the minor arc from \(C\) to \(D\), i.e. inside the original \(19^\circ\) angle. This marks points at central angles
   \[
   1^\circ,2^\circ,3^\circ,\dots,18^\circ,19^\circ.
   \]

5. Draw rays from \(O\) to the 18 interior marked points. These rays divide \(\angle AOB\) into \(19\) equal angles of \(1^\circ\) each.

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{l}
\text{Step the chord of the given }19^\circ\text{ angle 19 times around a circle centered at the vertex.}\\
\text{Since }19\cdot 19^\circ=361^\circ,\text{ the last ray is }1^\circ\text{ from the first.}\\
\text{Then step this }1^\circ\text{ chord across the original }19^\circ\text{ arc and draw the rays to the points;}\\
\text{these divide the angle into 19 equal parts.}
\end{array}
}
\]
